paragraphs.title: A Holy People to the LORD

easy.question: To whom is it said, “Ye are the children”?
answers: The LORD your God
The king of the land
All the nations
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Israelites are children of the LORD their God.

easy.question: What does the verse forbid doing for the dead?
answers: Weeping for them
Cutting yourselves and making baldness
Burying them
easy.explanation: The verse forbids cutting yourselves and making baldness between your eyes for the dead.

easy.question: How does the verse describe Israel?
answers: Only as a great nation
As a foreign people
As a holy and special people
easy.explanation: The verse describes Israel as a holy people and a peculiar, or special, people of the LORD.

medium.question: Why does the passage first say that Israel are children of the LORD before forbidding mourning practices?
answers: To teach that their identity affects their behavior even in mourning
To explain where the graves are
To tell about the birth of the Israelites
medium.explanation: The passage connects Israel’s relationship with the LORD to the proper way to behave when someone dies.

medium.question: In the phrase “make any baldness between your eyes for the dead,” what does “baldness” refer to?
answers: A special garment for mourning
Shaving or removing hair as a sign of mourning
The burial of the dead
medium.explanation: The context concerns an action performed on the body because of the dead, so baldness means creating a bare place in the hair as a mourning sign.

medium.question: How are the two verses connected?
answers: The second verse introduces a new geographical place
The first concerns the nations, and the second concerns burial
The first gives the practice being forbidden, and the second explains Israel’s special status
medium.explanation: The passage first forbids certain mourning practices and then explains that Israel is a holy and chosen people.

challenge.question: What does the word “For” at the beginning of the second verse show?
answers: That the prohibition is connected to Israel’s being holy and special
That the passage changes to another people
That the prohibition applies only to priests
challenge.explanation: “For” connects the prohibition in the first verse with its reason: Israel is a holy people chosen by the LORD.

challenge.question: What does “above all the nations that are upon the earth” emphasize?
answers: That Israel is the only people living in the world
That Israel was chosen from among all the nations
That only nations near Israel were chosen
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Israel was chosen from among all the peoples of the world.

challenge.question: What precise distinction follows from the prohibitions in the first verse?
answers: It is forbidden to feel sorrow for the dead
All mourning practices are allowed without limits
The verse restricts certain bodily actions but does not forbid mourning itself
challenge.explanation: The verse forbids cutting and making baldness, but it does not say that people may not grieve for the dead.

questions.question: What does the word “For” at the beginning of the second verse show?
answers: That the prohibition is connected to Israel’s being holy and special
That the passage changes to another people
That the prohibition applies only to priests
questions.explanation: “For” connects the prohibition in the first verse with its reason: Israel is a holy people chosen by the LORD.

questions.question: What does “above all the nations that are upon the earth” emphasize?
answers: That Israel is the only people living in the world
That Israel was chosen from among all the nations
That only nations near Israel were chosen
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Israel was chosen from among all the peoples of the world.

questions.question: What precise distinction follows from the prohibitions in the first verse?
answers: It is forbidden to feel sorrow for the dead
All mourning practices are allowed without limits
The verse restricts certain bodily actions but does not forbid mourning itself
questions.explanation: The verse forbids cutting and making baldness, but it does not say that people may not grieve for the dead.

easy.question: What does the passage forbid eating at the beginning?
answers: Any abominable thing
Only pork
Only fish
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing.”

easy.question: Which animal is listed among those that may be eaten?
answers: The camel
The ox
The swine
easy.explanation: The passage says that the ox, sheep, and goat may be eaten.

easy.question: What does the passage say about the swine?
answers: It may be eaten
It chews the cud
Its flesh may not be eaten
easy.explanation: The swine is unclean, so its flesh may not be eaten.

medium.question: Which combination of signs makes an animal fit to eat?
answers: Dividing the hoof only
Chewing the cud only
Dividing the hoof into two claws and chewing the cud
medium.explanation: The animal must part the hoof, divide it into two claws, and chew the cud.

medium.question: Why are the camel, hare, and coney forbidden?
answers: They chew the cud but do not divide the hoof
They divide the hoof but do not chew the cud
They are not animals
medium.explanation: The passage says that they chew the cud but do not divide the hoof.

medium.question: What does “their dead carcase” mean in “nor touch their dead carcase”?
answers: Their living flesh
Their body after death
Their hoof
medium.explanation: A dead carcase is the body of an animal after it has died.

challenge.question: What can be inferred by comparing the swine with the camel, hare, and coney?
answers: One sign is enough to make an animal clean
An animal that lacks all the required signs is unclean
Only animals that live in the wilderness are unclean
challenge.explanation: The swine has one sign, while the other animals have the other sign; all are unclean, so the signs are required together.

challenge.question: Which statement accurately follows the order of the passage?
answers: The signs of a clean animal are given first, followed by examples of unclean animals
The swine is forbidden first, and only afterward is anything permitted
Only animals that may not be touched are listed first, followed by fish
challenge.explanation: The passage first gives the requirements for a clean animal, then lists animals that do not meet them.

challenge.question: What special detail is stated about the swine compared with the animals in the previous verse?
answers: The swine does not divide the hoof at all
The swine both divides the hoof and chews the cud
The swine divides the hoof but does not chew the cud
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the swine divides the hoof but does not chew the cud.

questions.question: What can be inferred by comparing the swine with the camel, hare, and coney?
answers: One sign is enough to make an animal clean
An animal that lacks all the required signs is unclean
Only animals that live in the wilderness are unclean
questions.explanation: The swine has one sign, while the other animals have the other sign; all are unclean, so the signs are required together.

questions.question: Which statement accurately follows the order of the passage?
answers: The signs of a clean animal are given first, followed by examples of unclean animals
The swine is forbidden first, and only afterward is anything permitted
Only animals that may not be touched are listed first, followed by fish
questions.explanation: The passage first gives the requirements for a clean animal, then lists animals that do not meet them.

questions.question: What special detail is stated about the swine compared with the animals in the previous verse?
answers: The swine does not divide the hoof at all
The swine both divides the hoof and chews the cud
The swine divides the hoof but does not chew the cud
questions.explanation: The passage says that the swine divides the hoof but does not chew the cud.

easy.question: Which creatures in the waters may be eaten?
answers: Those with fins and scales
All creatures in the waters
Only creatures without scales
easy.explanation: Only creatures in the waters that have both fins and scales may be eaten.

easy.question: What may not be eaten according to verse 10?
answers: Creatures with fins and scales
Creatures without fins and scales
All animals on land
easy.explanation: The verse forbids anything that does not have fins and scales.

easy.question: Which two signs are mentioned?
answers: Wings and tails
Feet and horns
Fins and scales
easy.explanation: The two signs mentioned are fins and scales.

medium.question: What must be true for a creature in the waters to be eaten?
answers: It must have both fins and scales
It must have only fins
It must have only scales
medium.explanation: The rule requires both fins and scales.

medium.question: In the phrase “fins and scales,” what are scales?
answers: Organs used for swimming
Small plates covering the body of a fish
A part of a fish’s mouth
medium.explanation: Scales are the small plates that cover the body of a fish.

medium.question: What is the result when one of the two signs is absent?
answers: The creature immediately becomes permitted
Only its color must be examined
It may not be eaten
medium.explanation: The passage forbids creatures that do not have fins and scales, so lacking either sign makes them forbidden.

challenge.question: Which wording most accurately summarizes the rule?
answers: Both signs are required; one alone is not enough
One sign is enough
The signs do not matter if the creature lives in water
challenge.explanation: The first verse permits creatures with both signs, while the second forbids those lacking either one.

challenge.question: Why does “whatsoever” strengthen the prohibition?
answers: It limits the prohibition to one creature
It shows that the prohibition applies to everything lacking one of the signs
It turns the prohibition into a recommendation
challenge.explanation: “Whatsoever” broadens the rule and emphasizes that no creature lacking fins and scales is exempt.

challenge.question: What important point follows from the transition between verses 9 and 10?
answers: The second verse repeats the first without adding anything
The first verse concerns land and the second concerns water
The second verse gives the opposite side of the condition for permission
challenge.explanation: Verse 9 gives the condition for eating, and verse 10 explains that lacking the condition results in prohibition.

questions.question: Which wording most accurately summarizes the rule?
answers: Both signs are required; one alone is not enough
One sign is enough
The signs do not matter if the creature lives in water
questions.explanation: The first verse permits creatures with both signs, while the second forbids those lacking either one.

questions.question: Why does “whatsoever” strengthen the prohibition?
answers: It limits the prohibition to one creature
It shows that the prohibition applies to everything lacking one of the signs
It turns the prohibition into a recommendation
questions.explanation: “Whatsoever” broadens the rule and emphasizes that no creature lacking fins and scales is exempt.

questions.question: What important point follows from the transition between verses 9 and 10?
answers: The second verse repeats the first without adding anything
The first verse concerns land and the second concerns water
The second verse gives the opposite side of the condition for permission
questions.explanation: Verse 9 gives the condition for eating, and verse 10 explains that lacking the condition results in prohibition.

easy.question: What kind of birds may be eaten?
answers: Clean birds
All ravens
Every creeping thing that flies
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Of all clean birds ye shall eat.”

easy.question: Which bird appears in the list of birds that may not be eaten?
answers: The stork
The eagle
The lapwing
easy.explanation: The eagle is listed among the birds that may not be eaten.

easy.question: What does the passage say about “every creeping thing that flieth”?
answers: It may be eaten at night
It may be eaten if it is small
It is unclean and may not be eaten
easy.explanation: The passage says that every creeping thing that flies is unclean and may not be eaten.

medium.question: What connection is there between the opening and closing statements about birds?
answers: Both concern only ravens
Both state that clean birds may be eaten
Both forbid eating every bird
medium.explanation: The passage opens and closes by stating that clean birds may be eaten.

medium.question: What does “creeping thing that flieth” describe?
answers: A small or swarming flying creature
A large and powerful bird
A clean bird permitted as food
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a small or swarming flying creature, which the passage declares unclean.

medium.question: Why does the passage list many bird names in verses 12–18?
answers: To teach that all birds were created in the same way
To show that only water birds are forbidden
To give examples of birds that may not be eaten
medium.explanation: After giving the general permission to eat clean birds, the passage lists specific birds that are forbidden.

challenge.question: What notable structure appears in the passage?
answers: Permission at the beginning and end, with forbidden birds listed in between
Prohibition at the beginning and permission only in the middle
Only a list of permitted birds, with no prohibitions
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions clean birds at the beginning and end, while forbidden birds are listed in the middle.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the repeated phrase “after his kind”?
answers: The rule applies to the related kinds within that group
The bird is permitted only when male
The passage refers to only one particular bird
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the rule concerns the bird and related kinds belonging to the same group.

challenge.question: What is the difference between the bird list in verses 12–18 and verse 19?
answers: Verses 12–18 permit all birds, while verse 19 forbids only one
Verses 12–18 name specific birds, while verse 19 forbids every creeping flying creature
There is no difference
challenge.explanation: Verses 12–18 list particular birds, while verse 19 gives a general prohibition concerning every creeping thing that flies.

questions.question: What notable structure appears in the passage?
answers: Permission at the beginning and end, with forbidden birds listed in between
Prohibition at the beginning and permission only in the middle
Only a list of permitted birds, with no prohibitions
questions.explanation: The passage mentions clean birds at the beginning and end, while forbidden birds are listed in the middle.

questions.question: What can be understood from the repeated phrase “after his kind”?
answers: The rule applies to the related kinds within that group
The bird is permitted only when male
The passage refers to only one particular bird
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the rule concerns the bird and related kinds belonging to the same group.

questions.question: What is the difference between the bird list in verses 12–18 and verse 19?
answers: Verses 12–18 permit all birds, while verse 19 forbids only one
Verses 12–18 name specific birds, while verse 19 forbids every creeping flying creature
There is no difference
questions.explanation: Verses 12–18 list particular birds, while verse 19 gives a general prohibition concerning every creeping thing that flies.

easy.question: What may the Israelites not eat?
answers: Anything that dies of itself
Only fruit
Only fish
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye shall not eat of anything that dieth of itself.”

easy.question: What may be done with an animal that Israelites may not eat?
answers: It must only be buried
It may be given to a stranger or sold to an alien
It may be cooked with milk
easy.explanation: The verse permits giving it to a stranger in the gates or selling it to an alien.

easy.question: What may not be boiled?
answers: A lamb in water
A fish in oil
A kid in its mother’s milk
easy.explanation: The verse ends by forbidding boiling a kid in its mother’s milk.

medium.question: What two options does the verse give for the animal that died of itself?
answers: Give it to a stranger or sell it to an alien
Eat it or burn it
Cook it or hide it
medium.explanation: The verse says to give it to a stranger or sell it to an alien.

medium.question: What does “anything that dieth of itself” mean?
answers: A sweet food
An animal that died or meat not prepared in the permitted way
Well-roasted meat
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to an animal that died on its own or meat that was not prepared in the permitted way.

medium.question: What reason does the verse give for these instructions?
answers: To conserve food
To protect animals
Because Israel is a holy people to the LORD
medium.explanation: The verse explains that Israel is a holy people to the LORD, and therefore must follow these rules.

challenge.question: What difference does the verse make between the stranger and the alien?
answers: The animal is given to the stranger and sold to the alien
It is sold to the stranger and given freely to the alien
The verse makes no difference between them
challenge.explanation: The verse uses different instructions: give it to the stranger and sell it to the alien.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command “Thou shalt not seethe,” rather than only “Thou shalt not eat”?
answers: The dish may be eaten if it was not boiled
The prohibition includes the act of boiling itself
The prohibition applies only to a living kid
challenge.explanation: The command forbids the cooking action itself, not merely eating the finished dish.

challenge.question: What does “anything” emphasize in the phrase “anything that dieth of itself”?
answers: Only a kid that dies is forbidden
Only an animal found in the gates is forbidden
The prohibition applies to every animal that dies of itself
challenge.explanation: The wording broadens the prohibition to include any animal that dies on its own.

questions.question: What difference does the verse make between the stranger and the alien?
answers: The animal is given to the stranger and sold to the alien
It is sold to the stranger and given freely to the alien
The verse makes no difference between them
questions.explanation: The verse uses different instructions: give it to the stranger and sell it to the alien.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command “Thou shalt not seethe,” rather than only “Thou shalt not eat”?
answers: The dish may be eaten if it was not boiled
The prohibition includes the act of boiling itself
The prohibition applies only to a living kid
questions.explanation: The command forbids the cooking action itself, not merely eating the finished dish.

questions.question: What does “anything” emphasize in the phrase “anything that dieth of itself”?
answers: Only a kid that dies is forbidden
Only an animal found in the gates is forbidden
The prohibition applies to every animal that dies of itself
questions.explanation: The wording broadens the prohibition to include any animal that dies on its own.

paragraphs.title: Tithes and Eating before the LORD

easy.question: From what must a person give a tithe?
answers: From all the increase of his seed
Only from cattle
Only from sheep
easy.explanation: The verse commands tithing all the increase of the seed that the field produces.

easy.question: Where is the tithe to be eaten?
answers: In the field
Before the LORD at the place He chooses
In the king’s house
easy.explanation: The tithe is to be eaten before the LORD at the place He chooses.

easy.question: What is the purpose of eating before the LORD?
answers: To learn to fear the LORD
To increase the harvest
To choose a new place
easy.explanation: The verse says that the purpose is to learn to fear the LORD always.

medium.question: What does the list of things eaten before the LORD include?
answers: Only grain
Grain, wine, oil, and the firstlings of cattle and sheep
Only fruit and herbs
medium.explanation: The verse lists corn, wine, oil, and the firstlings of the herds and flocks.

medium.question: In the phrase “the tithe of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil,” what does “wine” represent?
answers: Wine or the produce of grapes
Cattle
The field
medium.explanation: In this list of agricultural produce, wine refers to the product of the grape harvest.

medium.question: Why must the person eat the tithe at the place chosen by the LORD?
answers: To learn to fear the LORD always
To keep away from the field
To keep all the produce for himself
medium.explanation: The verse connects eating at the chosen place with learning to fear the LORD throughout life.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the verse mentioning both agricultural produce and the firstlings of animals?
answers: The command concerns only farmers
Acknowledgment of the LORD includes different areas of a person’s livelihood
Raising animals is forbidden
challenge.explanation: The verse includes both field produce and livestock, showing that service to the LORD encompasses different sources of livelihood.

challenge.question: What does “always” emphasize at the end of the verse?
answers: Fear of the LORD should be a continual practice
The meal must be eaten on only one day
The tithe is given only once
challenge.explanation: “Always” shows that the purpose extends beyond a single event and calls for continual reverence for the LORD.

challenge.question: What relationship between the tithe and the chosen place appears in the verse?
answers: The tithe may be eaten anywhere without connection to worship
The tithe is brought to a central place chosen for worship
The tithe must remain in the field where it was produced
challenge.explanation: The verse connects eating the tithe with the place where the LORD chooses to place His name.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the verse mentioning both agricultural produce and the firstlings of animals?
answers: The command concerns only farmers
Acknowledgment of the LORD includes different areas of a person’s livelihood
Raising animals is forbidden
questions.explanation: The verse includes both field produce and livestock, showing that service to the LORD encompasses different sources of livelihood.

questions.question: What does “always” emphasize at the end of the verse?
answers: Fear of the LORD should be a continual practice
The meal must be eaten on only one day
The tithe is given only once
questions.explanation: “Always” shows that the purpose extends beyond a single event and calls for continual reverence for the LORD.

questions.question: What relationship between the tithe and the chosen place appears in the verse?
answers: The tithe may be eaten anywhere without connection to worship
The tithe is brought to a central place chosen for worship
The tithe must remain in the field where it was produced
questions.explanation: The verse connects eating the tithe with the place where the LORD chooses to place His name.

easy.question: What should a person do if the chosen place is too far away to carry the tithe?
answers: Sell it for money and carry the money
Leave it at home
Give it immediately to a Levite
easy.explanation: The passage commands him to sell the tithe, take the money, and go to the place chosen by the LORD.

easy.question: What may the person buy with the money at the chosen place?
answers: Only clothing
Cattle, sheep, wine, and strong drink
Only tools
easy.explanation: The passage lists oxen, sheep, wine, strong drink, and whatever the person desires.

easy.question: Whom must the person not forsake?
answers: The priest in the sanctuary
The poor person on the road
The Levite within the gates
easy.explanation: The passage says, “The Levite that is within thy gates; thou shalt not forsake him.”

medium.question: Why is it permitted to turn the tithe into money?
answers: Because the place is far away and the load is difficult to carry
Because the tithe may not be used as food
Because the Levite requested money
medium.explanation: The reason is that the journey may be too long and the tithe too difficult to carry.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the actions described?
answers: Eat, sell, travel, and buy
Take the money, bind it in hand, travel, and buy
Buy, bind, sell, and eat
medium.explanation: First the tithe is converted to money, then the money is carried to the chosen place, where purchases are made and eaten.

medium.question: In the phrase “thou art not able to carry it,” what does “carry” mean?
answers: See it
Keep it
Transport or bear it
medium.explanation: The context concerns a long journey and a heavy load, so “carry” means to bear or transport it.

challenge.question: What reason is given for not forsaking the Levite?
answers: The Levite has no part or inheritance with Israel
The Levite is responsible for selling the tithe
The Levite must travel with the person
challenge.explanation: The passage says not to forsake the Levite because he has no part or inheritance with the people.

challenge.question: What does “whatsoever thy soul lusteth after” teach about using the money?
answers: It may be used only to buy cattle
The person may choose among different foods and drinks and rejoice before the LORD
All the money must be given to the poor
challenge.explanation: The phrase broadens the permitted purchases and connects them with eating and rejoicing before the LORD with the household.

challenge.question: What does “there” emphasize in “thou shalt eat there before the LORD”?
answers: The meal must be eaten at the person’s home
The meal must be eaten on the way
The meal must be eaten at the place chosen by the LORD
challenge.explanation: “There” refers back to the place that the LORD has chosen, not to the person’s home.

questions.question: What reason is given for not forsaking the Levite?
answers: The Levite has no part or inheritance with Israel
The Levite is responsible for selling the tithe
The Levite must travel with the person
questions.explanation: The passage says not to forsake the Levite because he has no part or inheritance with the people.

questions.question: What does “whatsoever thy soul lusteth after” teach about using the money?
answers: It may be used only to buy cattle
The person may choose among different foods and drinks and rejoice before the LORD
All the money must be given to the poor
questions.explanation: The phrase broadens the permitted purchases and connects them with eating and rejoicing before the LORD with the household.

questions.question: What does “there” emphasize in “thou shalt eat there before the LORD”?
answers: The meal must be eaten at the person’s home
The meal must be eaten on the way
The meal must be eaten at the place chosen by the LORD
questions.explanation: “There” refers back to the place that the LORD has chosen, not to the person’s home.

paragraphs.title: The Tithe for the Poor in the Third Year

easy.question: When must the tithe of the increase be brought out and stored within the gates?
answers: Every year
In the third year
Only in the seventh year
easy.explanation: The passage says that at the end of three years the tithe is to be brought out and stored within the gates.

easy.question: Who comes to eat the tithe stored within the gates?
answers: Only the landowner
Only the priests
The Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow
easy.explanation: The passage names the Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow as those who may eat the tithe.

easy.question: What will happen when the needy are cared for?
answers: The LORD will bless the work of the person’s hands
The tithe will disappear
There will be no need to work
easy.explanation: The passage promises that the LORD will bless the work of the person’s hands.

medium.question: Why is the Levite specifically mentioned among those who eat the tithe?
answers: Because he has no part or inheritance with Israel
Because he is not allowed to eat grain
Because he is responsible for the city gates
medium.explanation: The passage explains that the Levite has no part or inheritance with the people.

medium.question: What does “at the end of three years” mean in context?
answers: At the beginning of the three years
At the close of a three-year cycle
In the middle of every year
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that the tithe is brought out at the completion of a three-year period.

medium.question: What is the connection between storing the tithe within the gates and the needy eating it?
answers: The tithe is stored in an accessible place so the needy can come and eat
The needy must take the tithe from the sanctuary
The tithe is stored within the gates so that no one will eat it
medium.explanation: The passage connects storing the tithe within the gates with the coming of the Levite and the needy to eat and be satisfied.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that responsibility does not end with setting aside the tithe?
answers: The tithe is to be stored within the gates, where needy people can reach it
The tithe belongs only to the owner of the produce
The tithe must remain in the field
challenge.explanation: Storing the tithe within the gates makes it practically available for the needy to come, eat, and be satisfied.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied”?
answers: Giving the needy only a small amount is enough
The goal is to provide enough food to satisfy them
Only the Levite may eat the tithe
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes not merely eating, but eating enough to be satisfied.

challenge.question: Which sequence correctly describes the main idea of the passage?
answers: Setting aside the tithe, storing it within the gates, feeding the needy, and receiving blessing
Receiving blessing, gathering the tithe, driving away the needy, and eating
Eating the tithe, planting the crop, storing it within the gates, and receiving the Levite
challenge.explanation: The passage first commands bringing out and storing the tithe, then the needy eat and are satisfied, followed by the promise of blessing.

questions.question: Which detail shows that responsibility does not end with setting aside the tithe?
answers: The tithe is to be stored within the gates, where needy people can reach it
The tithe belongs only to the owner of the produce
The tithe must remain in the field
questions.explanation: Storing the tithe within the gates makes it practically available for the needy to come, eat, and be satisfied.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied”?
answers: Giving the needy only a small amount is enough
The goal is to provide enough food to satisfy them
Only the Levite may eat the tithe
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes not merely eating, but eating enough to be satisfied.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the main idea of the passage?
answers: Setting aside the tithe, storing it within the gates, feeding the needy, and receiving blessing
Receiving blessing, gathering the tithe, driving away the needy, and eating
Eating the tithe, planting the crop, storing it within the gates, and receiving the Levite
questions.explanation: The passage first commands bringing out and storing the tithe, then the needy eat and are satisfied, followed by the promise of blessing.
